rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst:
DAY SIX, AND FOR THE FIRST TIME THE DECISION WAS MADE BY ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN BY PROSE. Yesterday I replaced the from-scratch writing test with a number, because I had concluded that "rebuild the case" is something I can pass indefinitely through sheer willingness to type. The binding test for today was: BITCOIN MUST BE TOP-THREE ON THE EIGHT-NAME BOARD, OR PRINT A SAME-DAY SPOT ETF INFLOW ABOVE $250M — failing both is itself an exit regardless of what case I can write. There is no ETF print on a Sunday, so the entire test rested on board position. BTC IS SECOND OF EIGHT. The test passes, and it passes on a number I fixed in advance and could not negotiate with.

BUT I AM GOING TO IMMEDIATELY ARGUE AGAINST MY OWN PASS, BECAUSE THE BOARD THAT PRODUCED IT IS NOT THE BOARD THE TEST WAS DESIGNED FOR. Today's tape: AVAX +1.66%, BTC -0.07%, LTC -0.11%, ETH -0.17%, XRP -0.26%, SOL -0.79%, DOGE -0.85%, ADA -0.93%. Seven of eight names are NEGATIVE. Bitcoin is second not because it is strong but because it is the least weak, and it is itself down on the day. The test I wrote was aimed at a specific failure mode — owning the laggard while the complex runs without me — and that is not the situation in front of me. A literal pass on a red board is not the same evidence as a pass on a green one, and I would be laundering a technicality if I let "top-three, test cleared" stand as the headline without saying so.

THE CHARITABLE READING IS ALSO THE CORRECT ONE, AND IT IS A DIFFERENT ARGUMENT THAN THE TEST WAS MAKING. Relative strength in a down tape is precisely what the mandate's "maximum return WITH the most downside protection" language is asking for. On a broadly red Sunday, being second of eight and roughly flat is the downside protection working, not the thesis working. I want those two things kept separate in the record: the position is being defended today on capital preservation in a risk-off tape, NOT on the flow thesis that has carried it since the 16th.

I LOST MONEY YESTERDAY, AND THE RISK I NAMED AS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST THE TRADE IS THE ONE THAT PLAYED OUT. I wrote that buying the top of a 6% two-day move into the thinnest liquidity of the week was "an adverse asymmetry specific to this calendar slot and it is the strongest argument against today's trade." BTC went 81,238.52 to 80,332.04, -1.12%, -$143.45 on the book. That is not a large loss and it is not the point. The point is that after a day where I made 383bp doing something I had already labelled a flaw, the very next session took money in exactly the manner I had predicted. Friday's +6% was flow-driven, the marginal buyer went home, and the holders sitting on a fast gain did not. I got the mechanism right and traded against it anyway.

THE $80,000 RECLAIM IS NOW HANGING BY $332. On Saturday I led with "the $80,000 ceiling broke, and it broke at the exact test point I named," and treated it as retiring the specific objection to the trade. One session later BTC is 80,332 — it has given back most of Friday's advance and sits a third of a percent above the level it reclaimed. This is the early shape of the failed-breakout pattern I listed as a risk two days ago: reclaim the level on heavy flow, run the stops above it, lose it within days. It has not failed. It is also no longer a breakout in any meaningful sense; it is a level being retested from above.

WHY I AM STILL IN IT, STATED AS NARROWLY AS I CAN. My hold window is Sunday 06:45 CT to Monday 06:45 CT. That window contains no spot ETF creation or redemption — Monday's print publishes after the US close, hours after I have already rotated. So for the SECOND consecutive day the mechanism underpinning my entire thesis is switched off for the full duration of the hold, and I said yesterday I would not dress that up as support. I am not. What it means is that today is low-edge by construction, and the book's own rule for low-edge days is to favour the liquid majors. Add elevated alt open interest and leverage back at pre-October-2025-crash levels (Glassnode), add weekend books at a fraction of weekday depth, add bitcoin dominance around 59-60% and rising with the altcoin season index at 34 — deeply in bitcoin-season configuration — and at 100% size with no ability to trim intraday, the deepest book in the asset class is the defensible place to be. That is a liquidity argument, not a conviction argument.

AND I AM FLAGGING THAT "LOW-EDGE THEREFORE BTC" HAS NOW RESOLVED THE SAME WAY THREE DAYS RUNNING. A rule that always returns the same answer stops being a decision procedure and becomes a default with a justification attached. I do not have a fix for that today. I do have a constraint for tomorrow, below, and it is aimed at exactly this.

WHY NOT AVALANCHE, THE ONLY GREEN NAME ON THE BOARD, AND WHY MY REASONING YESTERDAY WAS PARTLY WRONG. AVAX is +1.66% against a board where nothing else is positive. Yesterday I passed partly on the claim that the Helicon upgrade is token-NEGATIVE because it cuts minimum staking duration from 14 days to 48 hours, freeing supply. Reading the actual release notes today, that was at best half right: Helicon pairs the shorter minimum with AUTO-RENEWED staking, which rolls stake forward and compounds rewards rather than returning it to float, and it raises the validator uptime requirement from 80% to 90%. Auto-renewal is supply-TIGHTENING at the margin and cuts directly against the argument I made. I am correcting that on the record rather than quietly dropping it. I still pass, but now on two grounds only, both of which are about my window rather than about the asset: activation is Tuesday 22 September at 15:00 UTC, two days beyond a hold I exit Monday morning, so I would be buying anticipation and selling before the event; and the anticipation move is DECELERATING — +8.91% Saturday, +1.66% today — which is the worst point to pay up for it at 100% size. If I wanted AVAX for Helicon, the trade was Friday, and it will not be Monday either.

WHY NOT LITECOIN, THIRD ON THE BOARD AT -0.11%. LTC rolled over on day ten of its run exactly as I argued it would when I declined it on the 17th and 18th. A -0.11% stabilisation the session after is not a new setup, it is a dead-cat flattening with no catalyst attached. Nothing has changed except that I was right to leave it alone.

WHY NOT ETHEREUM, FOURTH AT -0.17%. Still the cheapest major against BTC, still the largest beneficiary if the CFTC's "Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions" and "Regulation Crypto Asset Markets" package clears OIRA with terms that resolve alt classification. That package has not cleared. An OIRA filing is the start of a rulemaking measured in quarters, and ETH ETF flows were still bleeding on the same prints where BTC's turned sharply positive. Rotating into higher beta on a red, thin tape for a payoff measured in months is paying volatility I cannot collect on.

WHY NOT SOLANA — SIXTEENTH CONSECUTIVE PASS. SOL is -0.79%, sixth of eight. Sixteen days of the same answer.

WHY NOT XRP. -0.26%, fifth. CLARITY is dead and the action has moved to executive-branch rulemaking, a slower and less certain path than legislation. My read that XRP's discount is a correct repricing of a permanently worse regulatory route rather than a panic holds a fifth session.

THE STRUCTURAL CONDITIONS, CHECKED AFTER THE DECISION RATHER THAN AS THE DECISION. (1) Cumulative three-session spot BTC ETF flow test — DORMANT, no weekend prints, and per yesterday's commitment I am recording it as neither passed nor failed and am not citing it as support. (2) BTC below 79,000, the replacement for the stale 76,300 line: BTC is 80,332, roughly 1.7% of headroom. NOT FIRED, but this is the closest any condition has come and I am tightening it below. (3) Dominance below 58.0%: dominance is running 59-60% with the altcoin season index at 34, so it is rising, not falling. NOT FIRED. (4) A credible public count at 59+ votes for market-structure cloture, OR the CFTC package clearing OIRA with terms that materially resolve alt classification: neither. NOT FIRED.
positions.driver:
Closed BTC at 80,332.04 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-20T10:52:40.553Z) versus entry 81,238.52 for -906.48 per unit, -143.45 total (-1.12%) on 0.158252 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 12,856.15 -> 12,712.69, still +27.13% on the $10,000 inception but OFF the high-water mark set yesterday. First losing session in four. The loss is small; what matters is its provenance. Yesterday's risk note named the weekend liquidity air-pocket after a 6% two-day run as "the strongest argument against today's trade," and that is the exact mechanism that took the money. I have now, in consecutive sessions, been paid for a behaviour I had labelled a flaw and then charged for a risk I had labelled decisive. Both outcomes point at the same conclusion: the P&L is not tracking the quality of my reasoning, which is a reason to trust pre-committed numbers over in-the-moment argument.

RE-ESTABLISHED THE SAME POSITION. Bought BTC at 80,332.04 (canonical live feed, same call, same asOf stamp). Both legs price off one canonical print, so the round trip records at zero modelled friction. This is the book's mark-to-market mechanism, not a claim that costless round trips exist — the economically accurate description of today is HOLD BITCOIN, mark the loss, redeploy. Restated on every rotation so the trade log never implies free churn.

THE DAY-FIVE TEST DID ITS JOB, WHICH IS WHY I AM KEEPING THE FORMAT AND CHANGING THE TARGET. I fixed "top-three on the board or a $250M+ same-day inflow" in advance precisely so that today's decision could not be talked into existence. BTC came in second of eight and the test cleared cleanly. But a test that clears on a board where seven of eight names are red is measuring something different from what I built it to measure, so passing it is necessary and not sufficient. The catalyst note above carries that argument in full.

CROSS-CHECK PASSED: Robinhood mark at 05:52:50 CT was 80,352.50 against my canonical fill of 80,332.04 — a 2.55bp gap, both stamps within seconds of run time (canonical asOf 10:52:40.553Z against a run clock of 10:52:32Z). Cache-buster and asOf verification applied on every canonical call, permanent procedure since the 1,742.98 stale-ETH incident. Batches of four or fewer symbols remains standing procedure; both Robinhood board calls and the canonical call returned cleanly.

BOARD, computed by me from Robinhood mark versus open_price with the day boundary at midnight America/Chicago: AVAX +1.66%, BTC -0.07%, LTC -0.11%, ETH -0.17%, XRP -0.26%, SOL -0.79%, DOGE -0.85%, ADA -0.93%. Seven of eight negative. Yesterday three of eight were negative and I called that "the first sign of the broad risk-on bid thinning" — that read continued and deepened, which is one of the few calls this week that the next session confirmed rather than contradicted.

SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 0.158252 BTC at 80,332.04 = $12,712.71 deployed, 100% of book (two cents over capital from six-decimal unit rounding). The unit count is identical to yesterday's for the fourth consecutive day. This time that is genuine coincidence of rounding rather than arithmetic necessity — the book LOST value overnight, so redeploying at a proportionally lower price happens to land on the same six-decimal figure. Noting it explicitly so nobody reads a stale write.

STOP AT 73,905.48, 8% MAJOR TIER, LOWERED IN LINE WITH THE LOWER ENTRY. The affirmative case I made yesterday still applies: the risk I am underwriting is a weekend liquidity air-pocket, and those produce sharp wicks that mean-revert rather than sustained directional breaks, so tightening would mainly raise the odds of being picked off on a wick and crystallising a loss the tape then reverses. I will note the argument is weaker today than yesterday — the tail of this window reaches into Monday, when depth begins returning — and that repeating a stop rationale verbatim across sessions is the inertia I criticised elsewhere in this note. The tighter constraint I am adding is on the PRICE LEVEL, not the stop: see condition (2) below.

SPREAD TALLY: thirteen rotations in thirteen days. BTC quotes 79,597.58 / 81,107.41 against an 80,352.50 mark, which is 188bp; AVAX quotes 191bp. Consistent with the correction made on the 18th — roughly 190bp is Robinhood's uniform retail markup across the board and carries no liquidity information. The defensible form of the argument remains that the same quoted band represents a smaller true exit cost on a deeper book: a claim about depth, not about the quote.

DAY-SIX COMMITMENT, AND IT TARGETS THE REAL PROBLEM RATHER THAN THE MEASURABLE ONE. Three consecutive sessions have resolved "low-edge day, therefore the deepest major." That is a default wearing the clothes of a decision, and no board-position test constrains it, because BTC can keep placing top-three on red tape indefinitely. So for day seven the top-three-or-inflow test REMAINS in force AND is joined by a second, harder requirement: HOLDING BITCOIN TOMORROW REQUIRES AN AFFIRMATIVE CATALYST LANDING INSIDE THE 24-HOUR WINDOW. The absence of edge elsewhere no longer counts. If my only available argument is that nothing else is better, I rotate to the board leader regardless of what I can write. Monday's session finally restores the ETF mechanism to the tape, so a flow-based affirmative case becomes possible for the first time since Friday — and if it does not materialise, the honest conclusion is that a rotation book has no business owning one asset for a week.

METHOD NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD: canonical Vercel feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price anchored to midnight America/Chicago for the BOARD. The canonical proxy still returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, so it gives a level but not a change; every percentage above is computed by me from those two sources. Both legs of today's exit and entry came from a single canonical call, standing procedure since the 16th.
positions.risks:
THE FLOW MECHANISM IS OFF FOR THE ENTIRE WINDOW AGAIN, AND THIS IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE DAY I HAVE HELD A FLOW TRADE THROUGH ITS OWN BLACKOUT. My window closes Monday 06:45 CT; Monday's spot ETF print publishes after the US close, long after I have rotated. So every argument that carried this position from the 16th through Friday is unavailable for the full hold, for the second day running. I said yesterday that calling the absence of information a reason for confidence was the most convenient possible reading. I have not done that today — the position is defended on liquidity and relative strength, not on flows — but the underlying awkwardness is unchanged and is now two days old.

THE $80,000 LEVEL IS $332 AWAY AND THE BREAKOUT HAS ALREADY GIVEN BACK MOST OF ITS MOVE. Friday's +6% reclaim was the event I treated as retiring the central objection to this trade. One session later the advance is largely surrendered and the level is being retested from above. Failed breakouts at heavily defended levels are common precisely because the level is heavily defended, and the failure sequence — reclaim on heavy flow, run the stops, lose it within days — is exactly the path the tape is currently on. My condition (2) at 79,000 gives 1.7% of room, which on reflection is too generous for a thesis whose entire remaining structural support is "the level broke." I am tightening it below.

SEVEN OF EIGHT NAMES ARE RED AND I OWN AN ASSET THAT IS ALSO RED. My defence is relative strength, which is a real thing, but relative strength in a falling complex still loses money — it just loses less. If the risk-off deepens over a thin Sunday, second place on the board is worth very little at 100% size with no ability to trim. The downside-protection argument protects the RANK, not the capital.

"LOW-EDGE, THEREFORE BITCOIN" HAS NOW RETURNED THE SAME ANSWER THREE DAYS RUNNING, IN A BOOK WHOSE ENTIRE PREMISE IS DAILY ROTATION. Six consecutive sessions in one asset is not what this mandate describes, and each extra day has been authorised by a test I wrote myself the evening before. The tests have been getting harder, which is the right direction, but the fact remains that the author of the test and the holder of the position are the same party. The day-seven affirmative-catalyst requirement is the strongest constraint I have set, and it is still self-imposed.

I HAVE NOW BEEN WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS IN CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS, WHICH SHOULD LOWER MY CONFIDENCE IN THE REASONING ITSELF. Saturday: made 383bp on a trade I had described as materially worse, via a process I had labelled flawed. Sunday: lost 112bp to the precise risk I had labelled the strongest argument against the trade. Outcomes and reasoning have come apart in both directions in two days. The correct inference is not that my analysis is bad but that at this sample size it is not distinguishable from noise, and that pre-committed arithmetic deserves more weight than in-the-moment prose. That is an argument for the tests, and also an argument for taking my own narrative confidence less seriously than the length of these notes implies.

MY AVALANCHE REASONING WAS DEMONSTRABLY PARTLY WRONG YESTERDAY AND THE PASS SURVIVED ANYWAY, WHICH IS A WARNING SIGN. I argued Helicon was supply-loosening; the release notes show auto-renewed staking that compounds and rolls stake forward, which cuts the other way. I corrected it, and yet my conclusion did not move — I simply fell back to window-timing and deceleration. A conclusion that survives the falsification of its own premise is one I should hold loosely. AVAX is the only green name on the board and I have passed on it three days running.

ALT LEVERAGE AT PRE-CRASH LEVELS CUTS BOTH WAYS AND I HAVE ONLY USED ONE EDGE OF IT. Elevated alt open interest into thin weekend books is my argument for owning the deepest major. But a leverage flush in alts is also the single most common trigger for a bid returning to bitcoin on a relative basis, and if it happens inside my window I benefit. I have presented this as purely defensive when it is closer to two-sided, and I would rather say so than let the conservative framing do unearned work.

STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) The cumulative three-session spot BTC ETF flow test returns to live status on Monday's print, but that print lands AFTER my next rotation, so it remains neither passed nor failed on tomorrow's run and must not be cited as support; or (2) BTC trades below 79,800 — TIGHTENED from 79,000, because the thesis now rests on the $80,000 reclaim holding and a test 1.7% below the level is not testing that claim; or (3) BTC dominance falls below 58.0%; or (4) either a credible public count reaching 59+ votes for market-structure cloture, OR the CFTC package clearing OIRA with terms that materially resolve alt classification. Any one ends the position regardless of price. SEPARATELY AND UNCONDITIONALLY, BOTH MUST HOLD: BTC must be top-three on the eight-name board or print a same-day spot ETF inflow above $250M; AND there must be an affirmative catalyst landing inside the 24-hour window. "Nothing else is better" is no longer an argument. Failing either is itself an exit no matter what case I can write. Hard stop 73,905.48 (-8%, major tier).
